pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: Walk me through your pipeline from a merged commit to running pods. What does each job do, what gates it, and what does it hand to the next one?
expected_points: test, then build-push, then deploy-dev, then deploy-prod, chained with needs — jobs run in parallel otherwise
build-push builds, tags the image from the commit, pushes it, and publishes the digest as a job output
each deploy job points its overlay at that artifact and applies it, then waits for the rollout
prod is gated on dev being green and on a GitHub environment (a required reviewer and the prod credentials)
failure modes named per stage: publishing an untested image without needs, a deploy that is never waited on, a tag that moved between push and deploy

questions.prompt: Your Deployment says `image: ghcr.io/ada/timesvc:latest`. You ship a bad release and run `kubectl rollout undo`. What happens, and what should the reference have been?
expected_points: the Deployment stores the image reference in the pod template and undo restores the previous template
with latest both revisions carry the same string, so the restored template is identical and nothing changes — the rollback silently no-ops
the tag has also moved, so re-pulling gets the bad image; with imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent different nodes can run different code under one name
use an immutable reference: a sha-<commit> tag, or better the digest, which is the image's content hash and cannot be moved

questions.prompt: Why does the prod job deploy the digest the dev job used, instead of rebuilding the same commit? And what is the one thing the deploy changes in the overlay?
expected_points: a rebuild of the same commit is a different image: base layers may have moved, cache and timestamps differ — dev proved the artifact, not the source
promotion means one artifact moving forward through environments
the deploy changes only the image reference (kustomize edit set image, or --set for a chart); replicas, resources, namespace and config already live in the overlay
the environments differ only where they are supposed to, so a diff between them is readable

questions.prompt: Your prod overlay raises the memory limit to 512Mi. What else has to change, what must not change, and why?
expected_points: GOMEMLIMIT is a literal in the base and follows nothing, so it has to move with the limit — under it, with headroom (roughly 80-90%)
GOMAXPROCS does not need touching if it reads limits.cpu through the downward API
the probes, the preStop sleep, terminationGracePeriodSeconds and the drain budget stay in the base so a fix reaches every environment
an overlay changes how much of something an environment gets, never whether the service works

questions.prompt: Your deploy step ran `kubectl apply` and the job is green. What have you actually proved, and which commands would prove the release landed?
expected_points: apply returns when the API server stored the object: nothing has been scheduled, pulled or probed
kubectl rollout status --timeout blocks until every replica is updated and available and exits non-zero on a stalled rollout (progressDeadlineSeconds)
then check what is running: the Deployment's image, and GET /version from a pod behind the Service, compared against the commit shipped
get pods for restart counts; a --timeout shorter than the job's so a bad release does not hold a runner

questions.prompt: Prod is serving a bad release. Take me through the rollback, how you know it worked, and what it does not undo.
expected_points: kubectl rollout undo restores the previous ReplicaSet's pod template, kept because of revisionHistoryLimit
it only works because the image reference is immutable and the two revisions differ
verify it: rollout status again, then the image and /version — the undo is a deploy and fails the same ways
pin the repository too (set the last good digest in the overlay) so the next apply does not reintroduce it
it does not undo anything outside the process — a schema migration, or data the bad version wrote

questions.prompt: List every credential your pipeline touches, where each lives, and why none of them is a password stored in the repository.
expected_points: github.token is minted per run and expires with it; packages: write is granted on the publishing job only, not workflow-wide
cluster credentials live in per-environment secrets, reaching the runner as ${{ secrets.NAME }}
OIDC (id-token: write) exchanges a signed claim about the workflow for a short-lived cloud credential, so there is nothing stored to leak or rotate
never in an image layer (layers are immutable and pullable), never in a committed manifest (base64 is not encryption and git remembers), never echoed by a step

questions.prompt: A cluster is gone. What in your repository lets you rebuild the service, and is git the record of what was running?
expected_points: namespace, then apply the overlay (kubectl apply -k / kustomize build / helm install), plus access to the image in the registry — including a pull secret if the package is private
the committed overlay names a bootstrap image reference, which must be immutable so a clean install lands on a known revision
the deploy job edits the overlay on the runner, so unless a step commits it back, the workflow run is the record and git is only a starting point
whichever you choose, the runbook has to say which one is authoritative and where to read the digest
